title: Prevent duplicate rig and skinned preview components
description:
## Summary
Make repeated editor preview binding converge on one owned `CreatureRig` and one owned `CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer` component on the preview root. The controller must define one deterministic owner for each generated component and its generated children rather than assuming `GetComponent<T>()` returns the only instance.

## Scope
- Audit both editor and runtime preview binding paths that create `CreatureRig` and `CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer`.
- Define one clear owner for each component and its generated children.
- Detect and remove duplicate components before binding, with deterministic cleanup semantics for their generated GameObjects and meshes.
- Preserve `TSK-0122` root ownership and do not replace it with name-based discovery.
- Add focused coverage for repeated binding/recovery where Unity execution is available.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Repeated editor preview binding leaves exactly one `CreatureRig` and one `CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer` on the owned preview root.
- Duplicate components created before binding cannot leave duplicate `Bone_*` or `SkinnedMesh` sibling hierarchies after cleanup.
- Cleanup does not destroy unrelated components or foreign children.
- The stale Unity-script-reference explanation remains an explicitly unverified hypothesis unless a Unity reproduction proves it.

## Validation
Run focused editor ownership tests and a repeated-binding/recovery check in Unity when available. Keep source inspection, automated validation, and Unity lifecycle validation separate.

## Current implementation
`CreaturePreviewController.GetSingleOwnedComponent<T>` scans owned components of each preview rig/skin type during bind/clear, clears generated state on the candidates, retains one deterministic component, and destroys duplicates. This is bind/reload-time only and does not add per-frame lookup or allocation.

## Status
InProgress — source hardening is present; Unity lifecycle validation remains the closure gate.
